translationRepairs: In the fourth year, the August Ancestor Gao died; Empress Dowager Lü summoned the king to Chang'an and killed him with poisoned wine.
In the fourth year [of Emperor Hui], after the August Ancestor Gao had died, Empress Dowager Lü summoned the king to Chang'an and killed him with poisoned wine.
The idiomatic field already resolves 四年 as Emperor Hui's fourth year. The literal field should make the same chronology clear and treat 高祖崩 as prior circumstance.
A clerk of the inner administration said, "The empress dowager values only the emperor and the Princess of Lu. You hold more than seventy cities, while the princess has barely a handful.
Shi, the clerk of the inner administration, said, "The empress dowager values only the emperor and the Princess Yuan of Lu. You hold more than seventy cities, while the princess has barely a handful.
士 is the clerk's personal name in 內史士曰, and 魯元公主 is Princess Yuan of Lu. The proposal restores both omitted name elements.
Luan Bo, returning from the campaign that had broken Qi, joined his command with others, diverted a river, and inundated the Zhao capital.
Luan Bu, returning from the campaign that had broken Qi, joined his command with others, diverted a river, and inundated the Zhao capital.
欒布 is conventionally romanized Luan Bu. The existing Luan Bo is an inconsistent name error.
Liu Jian, Prince Jian of Yan the Numinous.
Liu Jian, the Numinous Prince of Yan.
The heading gives Liu Jian's given name followed by his posthumous title 燕靈王. The proposal removes the erroneous construction 'Prince Jian.'
The ministers first considered the king of Qi, but objected in one voice: "His uncle Si Jun is vicious and overbearing—a man with a tiger's heart beneath a courtier's hat.
The ministers first considered the king of Qi, but objected in one voice: "His maternal uncle Si Jun is vicious and overbearing—a tiger in a courtier's hat.
The current translation's kinship identification is helpful and historically correct, while 虎而冠 is more directly a tiger wearing a cap. The revision preserves both points.
That year Prince Ai of Qi died, and his son Liu Ze, Prince Wen, succeeded him.
That year Prince Ai of Qi died, and his son Liu Ze, Prince Wen of Qi, succeeded him.
文王則 identifies Liu Ze as Prince Wen of Qi. Adding the full title prevents confusion without inserting a one-off parenthetical Chinese character into the English prose.
Soon Luan Bo and the Marquis of Pingyang arrived with other imperial columns, routed the besiegers, and raised the siege.
Soon Luan Bu and the Marquis of Pingyang arrived with other imperial columns, routed the besiegers, and raised the siege.
This is the same 欒布 name as in s0014 and should likewise read Luan Bu.
